strengths: The problem of competing with switching comparators without knowing the switching budget has a clear audience among researchers in adversarial bandits and online learning. The distinction from known-budget and stochastic settings is well motivated.

The logarithmic grid of candidate budgets and the master/base regret decomposition provide useful technical insight. In particular, the adaptive-base analysis explains how changing learning rates can produce square-root dependence on the inverse-probability threshold.

The progression from fixed-rate OMD to adaptive rates is pedagogically helpful, and the detailed appendices make the arguments inspectable. The manuscript also explicitly acknowledges that its uniform-mixing implementation is not covered by the stated analysis. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-8kl1hmbt/call-07c36231d34f4882bc8ee9ed4f63cb79/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: Necessary correction: The headline worst-case bound in Theorem 3.2 is not established for the stated Algorithm 2. Substituting η = √(H/T) into equation (14) gives the negative term −E[ρ_T(h†)]√T/(40√H log T). Equations (15) and (49) instead introduce an additional factor √K. Even granting the preceding lemmas, maximizing the correctly substituted expression over ρ yields only a bound of order SK√T up to logarithms, rather than the claimed S√(KT). This polynomial discrepancy cannot be hidden in logarithmic factors. The algorithm, proof, and theorem need a consistent learning-rate choice or a narrower guarantee.

Necessary correction: The variance-cancellation argument in Lemma A.4 contains an invalid step. Equation (46) cannot hold as written: with identically zero losses, no learning-rate increases occur, so its left side is zero while its right side is strictly negative because ρ_T(h†) = 2H. Moreover, the correction is asserted uniformly over comparator distributions p, although its magnitude depends on p(h†). The proof should fix an appropriate clipped unit comparator and account for initialization. It also defines G as negative entropy on page 18 while subsequently using the log-barrier divergence. These issues require a corrected derivation of the lemma; they do not by themselves establish that the lemma is false.

Necessary correction: Algorithm 1's feasible set can be empty. Its choice α = K^(1/3)/(T^(1/3)H^(1/2)) requires Hα ≤ 1, equivalently T ≥ KH^(3/2), but no such restriction is stated. For example, T = 1000 and K = 100 give H = 8 and Hα approximately 1.31. The algorithm needs a feasible parameter choice or an explicit restriction with the remaining cases handled.

Optional improvement: Describe ρ precisely as an algorithm-dependent threshold controlling inverse selection probabilities. It is an upper bound relevant to estimator variance, rather than the variance itself. Explaining when the ρ-dependent guarantee improves on the worst-case guarantee would make the result easier to interpret without requiring a stronger theorem.

Optional improvement: Provide an implementation procedure for the exact constrained updates with changing learning rates. Remark 3.6's cumulative-loss formulas do not directly specify these adaptive updates, and its acknowledged uniform-mixing heuristic leaves readers without a concrete implementation covered by the analysis.
